entry.narrative_markdown:
## Question
Who were the parents of John Richardson (tree person LR9N-VGQ, an LDS pioneer who died at Richmond, Cache, Utah, 10 March 1906), as shown by the Ashton-under-Lyne christening register?

## Conclusion (probable)
The evidence indicates that John Richardson was the son of **Thomas Richardson** (a spinner who signed by mark) and **Mary Richardson, born Mallalieu**, who married on 12 November 1826 at St Leonard, Walton le Dale, Lancashire. The tree already links John to these parents (ParentChild R28 and R29, now marked Biological). The conclusion is probable rather than proved because the link from the 1832 Ashton baptism to the Utah pioneer rests on name, day, month and place, and because the dates disagree (below).

## Evidence
**1. Original baptism register.** St Michael and All Angels, Ashton-under-Lyne, baptism register, entry no. 2040, 25 September 1832: John, son of Thomas X Richardson, Spinner, and Mary, officiating curate J. Hardman. Original record, primary information recorded by the curate in the course of duty, direct evidence of parentage. Mary's maiden name is not given. Citation: "England, Lancashire, Parish Registers 1538-1910," digital image, FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org : accessed 22 July 2026), St Michael and All Angels, Ashton-under-Lyne, baptism register, pp. 254-255, entry no. 2040, John, son of Thomas Richardson and Mary, 25 September 1832; citing original register held at Lancashire Record Office, Preston; FHL microfilm 4421674.

**2. Derivative index.** "England, Births and Christenings, 1538-1975" (collection 1473014) indexes the same christening (25 Sep 1832) naming Thomas Richardson and Mary. Derivative, secondary; it agrees with the image and adds nothing independent. Citation: "England, Births and Christenings, 1538-1975," database, FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:2:9H1K-BYQ : 4 February 2023, Entry for John Richardson, 25 Sep 1832); citing index based upon data collected by the Genealogical Society of Utah, Salt Lake City; FHL microfilm.

**3. Parents' marriage, original register.** St Leonard, Walton le Dale marriage register, p. 228, entry no. 684: Thos Richardson (Bachelor) and Mary Mallalieu (Spinster), married by banns 12 November 1826, both signing by mark, witnesses John Quarmen and James Townson, Rev. Henry Fielden. Original, primary, direct for the marriage, indirect for John's parentage: it supplies Mary's maiden name and shows a Thomas and Mary Richardson were a married couple six years before the baptism. Citation: "England, Lancashire, Parish Registers 1538-1910," digital image, FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:S3HY-6PR3-4VC : accessed 22 July 2026), St Leonard, Walton le Dale, marriage register, p. 228, entry no. 684, Thos Richardson and Mary Mallalieu, 12 November 1826; citing original register held at Lancashire Record Office, Preston; FHL microfilm. An indexed version (src_002, derivative) agrees.

## Reasoning and weaknesses
The identification of the baptized John with the Utah pioneer, and of the baptism's Thomas and Mary with the Mallalieu marriage, are correlations, not stated facts.
- Thomas and Mary Richardson of the baptism are tied to the 1826 couple by matching names, the husband signing by mark in both registers, and the nearby parishes (Walton le Dale adjoins Preston, the tree's birthplace). Richardson is a common surname and Thomas and Mary are common names, so this is suggestive, not conclusive. No record gives a child of the 1826 couple by name other than this baptism.
- **Date discrepancy (not registered as a conflict).** The original register says 1832. The tree has christening 25 September 1833 (fact fa26a9c0, cited to S4) and birth 24 July 1833 at Preston (fact 4bed1d6e; no linked source entry in research.json). A birth in July 1833 cannot follow a christening in September 1832, so either the tree's year is wrong or the baptized John is a different child. The same day, month and parish favor an error in the tree's year, but this has not been settled. I did not change the tree's christening fact, because the corrected date would sit before the stated birth; the birth date, the birthplace (Preston vs Ashton) and the year need to be examined and, if they stay in dispute, registered with conflict-resolution.
- All christening-sourced assertions come from one baptism event, so the sources are not independent for John's parentage.

## Tier
Probable. Direct primary evidence from an original register names both parents, and a second original register supplies a consistent maiden name, with no contrary candidate. It is not proved: identity of the baptized child with the subject rests on partial matches, the year disagrees, and research is not declared exhaustive. Unsearched records are listed in the search summary; a Utah death record or obituary naming parents, or a Preston-area birth or baptism entry, would test the identity link.

Citation: "England, Lancashire, Parish Registers 1538-1910," digital image, FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org : accessed 22 July 2026), St Michael and All Angels, Ashton-under-Lyne, baptism register, pp. 254-255, entry no. 2040, John, son of Thomas Richardson and Mary, 25 September 1832; citing original register held at Lancashire Record Office, Preston; FHL microfilm 4421674.

**2. Derivative index.** "England, Births and Christenings, 1538-1975" (collection 1473014) indexes the same christening (25 Sep 1832) naming Thomas Richardson and Mary. Derivative, secondary; it agrees with the image and adds nothing independent. Citation: "England, Births and Christenings, 1538-1975," database, FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:2:9H1K-BYQ : 4 February 2023, Entry for John Richardson, 25 Sep 1832); citing index based upon data collected by the Genealogical Society of Utah, Salt Lake City; FHL microfilm.

**3. Parents' marriage, original register.** St Leonard, Walton le Dale marriage register, p. 228, entry no. 684: Thos Richardson (Bachelor) and Mary Mallalieu (Spinster), married by banns 12 November 1826, both signing by mark, witnesses John Quarmen and James Townson, Rev. Henry Fielden. Original, primary, direct for the marriage, indirect for John's parentage: it supplies Mary's maiden name and shows a Thomas and Mary Richardson were a married couple six years before the baptism. Citation: "England, Lancashire, Parish Registers 1538-1910," digital image, FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:S3HY-6PR3-4VC : accessed 22 July 2026), St Leonard, Walton le Dale, marriage register, p. 228, entry no. 684, Thos Richardson and Mary Mallalieu, 12 November 1826; citing original register held at Lancashire Record Office, Preston; FHL microfilm. An indexed version (derivative) agrees.

## Reasoning and weaknesses
The identification of the baptized John with the Utah pioneer, and of the baptism's Thomas and Mary with the Mallalieu marriage, are correlations, not stated facts.
- Thomas and Mary Richardson of the baptism are tied to the 1826 couple by matching names, the husband signing by mark in both registers, and the nearby parishes (Walton le Dale adjoins Preston, the tree's birthplace). Richardson is a common surname and Thomas and Mary are common names, so this is suggestive, not conclusive.
- **Date discrepancy (not registered as a conflict).** The original register says 1832. The tree has christening 25 September 1833 (fact fa26a9c0, cited to S4) and birth 24 July 1833 at Preston (fact 4bed1d6e; no linked source entry in research.json). A birth in July 1833 cannot follow a christening in September 1832, so either the tree's year is wrong or the baptized John is a different child. The same day, month and parish favor an error in the tree's year, but this has not been settled. I did not change the tree's christening fact, because the corrected date would sit before the stated birth; the birth date, the birthplace (Preston vs Ashton) and the year should be examined and, if they stay in dispute, registered with conflict-resolution.
- All christening-sourced assertions come from one baptism event, so the sources are not independent for John's parentage.

## Tier
Probable. Direct primary evidence from an original register names both parents, and a second original register supplies a consistent maiden name, with no contrary candidate. It is not proved: identity of the baptized child with the subject rests on partial matches, the year disagrees, and research is not declared exhaustive. A Utah death record or obituary naming parents, or a Preston-area birth or baptism entry, would test the identity link.

**Patrick Flynn's Parentage (q_001)**

**Father — Probable:** Thomas Flynn is Patrick Flynn's most likely father. Patrick appears in Thomas's household in the 1850 and 1860 censuses, and Patrick's 1908 death certificate names Thomas as his father. These records carry some weight, but both are limited: the censuses record household position only (no explicit parent-child statement), and the death certificate's informant was a son-in-law — a secondary informant who was not present at Patrick's birth.

**Mother — Not Proved:** A widow named Bridget Flynn was considered, but the identity-match score is effectively zero (0.0002). Nothing connects her to this family beyond a shared surname and her 1870 widowhood. No mother link was written to the tree.

entry.narrative_markdown:
# Parents of Patrick Flynn (b. ~1845, d. 1908, Schuylkill County, Pennsylvania)

## Conclusion

The evidence indicates, at a **probable** level, that Patrick Flynn's father was **Thomas Flynn** (born about 1818, Ireland). The identity of his **mother** is **not proved**: a Bridget Flynn has been considered and is not supported by the evidence gathered so far.
